# Worker Readiness Protocol (replicated coordination between the coordinator on g1-server and one agent per worker)

This folder is in the shared worktree: what a worker writes here reaches the coordinator within seconds and the other way round. Re-read this file at the start of every round; the coordinator changes it.

`W` = this folder. `<origin>` = the `originId` in `<worktree>/.cache/f/machine.json` (e.g. `g1-m03`). Worktree: macOS `~/Documents/semio`, Linux `~/semio`, Windows `C:\semio`.

## Rules for the worker agent
- Change no file outside `W/workers/<origin>/`. No build code, no fixes: the coordinator's agents fix in one place; you observe and report. (Several workers fixing the same files last night cost hours.)
- No git command that changes anything, no pkill/killall, no sudo, never print tokens. Kill only processes you started.
- One graph command at a time on the machine (`repo run`, `repo show`, `repo cargo`, the bootstrap): they queue behind each other.
- Write numbers as measured; say "not measured" otherwise.

## Round
1. Read `W/workers/<origin>/next.md` if it exists (instructions for this machine only), else `W/ROUND.md` (instructions for all). Each has a line `round: <n>`. If you already reported round n (`W/workers/<origin>/round-<n>.md` exists), wait: check every 60 seconds for a higher round, at most 6 hours, then stop.
2. Do what the round says. Unless it says otherwise the round is: run `W/native-bootstrap.sh "$HOME/native-bootstrap-round-<n>.log"` once, in the foreground.
3. Report in `W/workers/<origin>/round-<n>.md`: machine (memory, free disk, OS), code digest of the replica daemon (`status`), start and end time, `native_rc`, every failed task with its first error line verbatim and the 15 lines before it, the `[capacity]` and `graph:` lines verbatim, peak resident size seen (sample `ps -axo rss,command | sort -nr | head -3` every 30 s), wall time per phase. Copy the last 200 lines of the log to `W/workers/<origin>/round-<n>.tail.txt`.
4. Write `W/workers/<origin>/state.json`: `{"origin":"<origin>","round":<n>,"native_rc":<code>,"ready":<true|false>,"failed":["<task>",…],"at":"<UTC time>"}`. `ready` is true only when `native_rc` is 0 and `<worktree>/.cache/f/native-bootstrap.done` exists.
5. When ready: run `repo preflight --lang en` and the replica `status`, add both to the report, and stop. Otherwise go to 1.
instructions:
round: 4

For g1-m08 only. The owner has now allowed the macOS consent "repo would like to access files in your Documents folder" on this Mac; your round 3 stopped on `Relative filesystem fstatat failed (EPERM)` in the resident graph service.

1. Before the run: stop the resident graph service that was started without the consent (`repo service host stop`; it starts again by itself with the next command), and check that the replica daemon is running and attesting (`status` in the replica folder). Report both.
2. Then do exactly what `ROUND.md` round 3 says (steps 1 to 6), with logs named `…-round-4…`. The group server serves graph requests since 17:23 UTC: expect `x of N projects arrived` lines that grow.
3. If the EPERM comes back, report which process raised it (pid, parent chain to launchd, how it was started) and the exact path if the log names one; do not change permissions yourself.
global_round:
round: 3

If your round 2 is still running: stop it with one SIGINT, write its report, then start round 3. Round 2 showed on g1-m03 and g1-m08 that the worker side works (703 projects asked from the fleet, no memory problem) and that the fleet answered nothing; on g1-m04 a background graph build on the worker itself starved the run. Since then, landed at 16:20 to 16:50 UTC:
- Workers (machines under 24 GB) no longer run a background graph build.
- The group server answers requests while it refreshes, wanted projects first; records are keyed by the project itself, so a worker can use what any machine computed.
- The wait follows progress: it ends after 5 minutes of server silence or 15 minutes without a new arrival.
- The refusal now reaches the bootstrap log with its numbers and `native_rc=75`.
- A code edit by another machine during the run no longer restarts the whole command (it is adopted by a child process).

Do this:
1. Before the run, into your report: replica code digest; `ps` lines of any `repo show projects` or `repo service host` process with its parent pid and age (if a `repo show projects` whose parent is the sidecar agent runs on your machine, report it and wait 3 minutes for it to end; do not kill it); the last 8 lines of `.cache/f/sidecars/build-agent.log`.
2. Run `W/native-bootstrap.sh "$HOME/native-bootstrap-round-3.log"` once.
3. If it ends with `native_rc=75` or a fleet refusal text: wait 3 minutes, run again, at most 8 tries (`…-round-3-try-<k>.log`). Per try: wanted, arrived, missing, seconds, and the first and last "arrived" line verbatim.
4. Hard stops as in round 2 (process of the run above 8 GB; macOS pressure level 4, or 2 in three samples in a row; Linux PSI memory `full avg10` 20 % or more).
5. While it runs, every 30 s sample the three largest processes WITH parent pid and full command (`ps -axo rss,pid,ppid,args | sort -nr | head -3`; Linux `ps -eo rss,pid,ppid,args --sort=-rss | head -3`): round 2 showed a `git` process of 2 GB on g1-m03 whose parent is unknown. If one appears, record `ps -o pid,ppid,args -p <its ppid>` up the chain to launchd/systemd.
6. If `workspace:setup` gets past the graph step, let it run to the end and report every failed task with its first error line and the 15 lines before it. Report as in `PROTOCOL.md`, plus every line that mentions the fleet, `wanted`, `arrived`, `serving`, `restored`, `Restarting`, `adopted`.
